findings.title: Team admins and owners are checked as if they must be both
findings.body: The permission check combines `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` with `&&`. These are alternative team roles, so a normal admin or owner will fail this check and be denied access unless they also hold the other role. Use an OR check to allow either role.

findings.title: Calendar updates use the caller's credentials instead of the booking owner's
findings.body: This endpoint allows attendees and team admins to add guests, but it loads credentials for `ctx.user` and supplies them to the calendar event manager. For those callers, these are not necessarily the credentials for the booking owner's calendar, so the provider update can target the wrong account or fail; the newly added guests may then be missing from the actual calendar event.

findings.title: Guest-add notifications ignore disabled standard-email settings
findings.body: This email path sends organizer and attendee notifications unconditionally and does not accept or check the event type metadata used by the standard email senders to honor `disableStandardEmails.all.host` and `.attendee`. Events configured to disable standard emails will still send these notifications when guests are added, contrary to that setting.

findings.title: Email classification uses the unfiltered guest input
findings.body: The handler filters existing attendees out of `uniqueGuests`, but passes the original `guests` input to `sendAddGuestsEmails`. That sender treats every attendee whose email is in this list as newly invited and sends them a normal scheduled-booking email. If a request includes an existing attendee alongside a new address, the existing attendee receives the wrong email; pass the filtered list instead.

findings.title: Guest blacklist checks can be bypassed with email casing
findings.body: Blacklist entries are lowercased when loaded, but the submitted `guest` is compared without normalization. Submitting a blacklisted address with different casing (for example, an uppercase domain) bypasses the configured blacklist and creates the attendee. Normalize both sides before checking.

findings.title: A calendar-sync failure leaves guests saved without notifications
findings.body: The attendee rows are committed by the booking update before this external calendar operation runs. If `updateCalendarAttendees` rejects, the mutation returns an error and never reaches the email send, even though the guests are already saved. Retrying the same request then finds no new guests and rejects it, so the missing calendar update and notifications cannot be retried through this endpoint.
